extraction.name: The F LORES -101 Evaluation Benchmark for Low-Resource and Multilingual Machine Translation
extraction.description: The FLORES-101 evaluation benchmark, consisting of 3001 sentences extracted from English Wikipedia and covering a variety of different topics and domains.
extraction.creator: Naman Goyal, Cynthia Gao, Vishrav Chaudhary, Peng-Jen Chen, Guillaume Wenzek, Da Ju, Sanjana Krishnan, Marc'Aurelio Ranzato, Francisco Guzman, Angela Fanyz
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The sentences in FLORES-101 were extracted from English Wikipedia, specifically from Wikinews, Wikijunior, and WikiVoyage. The selection process consisted of selecting an article at random from each source, and then manually selecting a few contiguous sentences from each article.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The translations were created by professional translators through a carefully controlled process. The workflow consisted of two parts: translation (which includes editing), performed by an initial LSP, and quality assurance (QA) performed by an independent LSP.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The translation quality score was determined based on the number of identified errors by the evaluation LSPs. The following errors were examined: grammar, punctuation, spelling, capitalization, addition or omission of information, mistranslation, unnatural translation, untranslated text, and register.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: 10 different annotators in the lab, 6 male and 4 female; with different roles in research: researchers (scientists and engineers) and program/project managers; originally coming from different regions of the world: East Asia, South Asia, Southern Europe, Latin America and North America
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is publicly released and will be maintained through versioning information in terms of the updating timeframe, the maintainers, and the deprecation policies.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset enables better assessment of model quality on the long tail of low-resource languages, including the evaluation of many-to-many multilingual translation systems.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The translations were checked for copying from popular translation engines, and a heuristic was proposed to detect and reject professional translations that are likely copies from translation engines.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The largest error category across all languages was mistranslation, a broad error category that generally notes that the source text was not translated faithfully and the translation has rendered an incorrect meaning in the target language.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset can be used for training, testing, validation, and fine-tuning of machine translation models. It supports many-to-many evaluation, document-level translation, and multimodal translation evaluation.
